hints.title: Binary Decision Tree Obstacle
hints.text: Every element in an array has two choices for any given subset: it is either included or excluded. How can systematic branching explore all combinations without duplicate subsets?

hints.title: Prefix Expansion Invariant
hints.text: Generate combinations by deciding whether to include each element at each index, or by expanding partial subsets from a starting index forward.

hints.title: State Tree Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an empty result list. Define a recursive exploration function taking the current index and current path. At each step, append a copy of the current path to the result. Then loop through candidate indices from the current index to the end, append nums[i] to path, recurse with i + 1, and pop from path to revert state.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def subsets(self, nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
        res = []
        path = []
        def backtrack(start):
            res.append(list(path))
            for i in range(start, len(nums)):
                path.append(nums[i])
                backtrack(i + 1)
                path.pop()
        backtrack(0)
        return res
```

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10)
complexity.notes: Produces all 2^N subsets, each of average length N/2.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^N subsets cannot be done faster than O(2^N) because 2^N distinct subsets must be produced.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place path modification uses O(N) call stack and path memory instead of copying arrays at every branch.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean state restoration (push and pop), copy creation when storing into result (path[:] or list(path)), understanding the 2^N state tree size.

solutions.approach: Backtracking State Tree with In-Place Push/Pop
